result.rationale: The diff line `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js does use substring matching rather than an exact origin comparison, exactly as the finding describes. An origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl would pass the check, weakening the security of the postMessage handler. Impact is limited to iframe resizing (accepted message only sets height), but the mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The postMessage origin check uses substring matching, not an exact origin comparison. `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured discourseUrl — e.g. with discourseUrl `http://discourse.example.com`, a page at origin `http://discourse.example` (or any attacker controlling a domain that is a prefix of it) can drive iframe sizing. Should compare against an exact origin (e.g. a dedicated discourseOrigin variable).

adjudication.rationale: In newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the `message` handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is not an exact origin match; any origin that is a prefix/substring of `discourseUrl` (e.g. `http://discourse.example` when `discourseUrl` is `http://discourse.example.com`) will pass the check and can send `discourse-resize` messages to control the iframe height. The finding accurately describes a security/correctness issue introduced by this diff.
